title: Kensho Residence: a Japanese garden on a narrow Taman Desa site.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #477 | KENSHO RESIDENCE, TAMAN DANAU DESA
excerpt: A boutique tower of about 300 units squeezed onto a small commercial plot in Taman Danau Desa, with a Japanese garden theme and shops on the doorstep. Sean likes the detailing and the layout but warns of busy streets and an uncertain plot next door.
takeaways: About 300 units on a narrow plot, with a ramped car park and a Japanese tea garden theme.
A 1,034 sq ft corner unit lists at about RM800,000 and rents for up to about RM3,500 furnished.
Busy streets, a contested plot in front and many new projects nearby.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Kensho Residence fits about 300 units on a small, narrow plot. Cars park along a single continuous ramp from the ground floor to level seven, and the tower cantilevers over the level-eight deck, shading a pool, a two-storey jungle gym, an onsen-style hot pool and a jacuzzi. A Japanese tea garden theme of pebbles, stone and bonsai runs from the lobby to the rooftop.

Three lifts serve 10 units a floor, along a 2.1 m corridor. Sean viewed a 1,034 sq ft corner unit with three bedrooms, two bathrooms, a separate yard and utility room, Electrolux appliances, American Standard fittings and air-conditioners included.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: It sits in Taman Danau Desa, reached from Old Klang Road, the Middle Ring Road and the Sungai Besi Highway, beside a petrol station and two rows of shops, with two secondary schools nearby. It is car-dependent: the nearest station is Kuchai Lama. A former playground in front has been gazetted for development, possibly a tower of about 50 storeys, which residents are contesting, and some residents say a nearby open sewage pond smells on rainy days.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: On listings sites this leasehold unit is about RM800,000, about RM800 psf, and a fully furnished unit of this size rents for up to about RM3,500 a month. Sean expected higher rents and puts the gap down to competition from older and newer blocks around it; at a purchase price nearer RM700,000, the rent would still cover the instalment.

standout.title: No corner left undressed
standout.body: Even the landscape islands and service corners that most projects leave bare are dressed with chosen pebbles, plants and stone, in keeping with the Japanese garden theme. An overflowing water feature helps mask the street noise around the facilities.

pros: The Taman Desa address, near where Sean lives: mature amenities and a long-settled community, so a new owner immediately knows the schools, roads and places to eat. It is car-dependent, with Kuchai Lama the nearest station, but nobody seems to mind.

The architecture on a narrow site: seven storeys of ramped parking as the most cost-effective option, a Japanese tea garden theme from the lobby up, and a compact deck that uses every inch, with a spacious gym and the lifts placed on the least premium side.

A thoughtful layout: a 1,000 sq ft unit with a wet kitchen, yard and utility room is unusually generous at the back, and switches, kitchen cabinets, air-conditioners and American Standard fittings all come with it.
cons: The micro site: the streets below are busy and the traffic heavy, so it suits people who want convenience on foot, not quiet. The former playground in front may become a tower, a petrol station and older apartments sit beside it, and the mature roadside trees are being cut for development.

Design quirks: everyone parks on a ramp, visitors need a key card to come down from their parking floor, and the spaces are packed tightly from guardhouse to deck. In the unit, a door in the middle of the kitchen leaves it awkward, because the wall is meant to be knocked through, and the master bedroom is tight; the generous back of house only works in a corner unit.

Constant new supply: Kuchai Lama, Old Klang Road, Taman Desa, Puchong and Bukit Jalil always seem to have around 15 projects coming up, which crowds the roads at peak hours and frustrates long-time residents.

closing: Sean says he wouldn't mind living here with his family himself: a compact, well-detailed home for people who value walking to everything over peace and quiet.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this October 2026 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. A long-time viewer let Sean view his newly bought home; the price and rent are from listings sites as Sean quoted them. Sean mentions that he lives nearby.
